chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: Back at the Chez Florence, and Cuban Pete the con man
summary: He played again at the Chez Florence, where upstairs parties went on, and worked with an Algerian bandleader calling himself Cuban Pete.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So they were angry, too. So all right, I see all this happening. So I started gigging around with a few friends, you know, that I knew. We was playing Erico's Creole Band, started gigging with him. And I went to the old place I used to work, it's called the Chez Florence, where Louis used to be. And this woman recognizes me and says, I want you to make a band. And I was hurting, too. And she had an apartment there, she had a apartment.

Now, I didn't know that -- I was playing downstairs and I could see how those people would go back in there and everything, upstairs, there'd be parties up there, and they'd be doing business. Those kings and things would disappear and they'd be up there having their smoke.

And (inaudible) just downstairs. So I stayed there. And they had a boy from Tunisia, I believe, or Algeria. He was the greatest con man I've ever seen. He used to call himself Cuban Pete. Now, Cuban Pete couldn't do nothing. Because Algerians you have to watch them, he looks like Puerto Rican, looks like you, looks like everybody. And he'd tell you, 'I'm from Chicago.' And if you don't watch him, he'll get you.
And you can say, well, yes, okay. But he is not that man, he is entirely different. He is a Moslem and he has no compulsion about getting you because if you're not into this.
That's in the Koran, they've got a double standard.
You're one of the infidels. They can enslave do anything, they can slay you, they can beat you out of money, anything.
